newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ says NZ job ads down 2.6 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says NZ job ads down 2.6 pct in August.

text.p: ANZ Banking Group on Tuesday reported job advertisements in New Zealand's three main centres fell in August, continuing a four month trend.
The bank said job advertisements were a leading or coincident indicator and the recent falls reinforced its belief economic activity slowed further during the first half of 1996.
The job advertisement series showed a fall of 2.6 percent in August from July, while the August 1995 to August 1996 figures showed a 6.4 percent decline.

The ANZ estimates production-based GDP growth fell from a peak of 6.6 percent in the June 1994 year to 2.3 percent in the June 1996 year. The bank forecasts growth will reach a trough in the latter half of 1996.

All three main centres showed similar falls in August with job advertisements in the country's biggest city Auckland off 2.6 percent after a 2.6 percent fall in July. Advertisements in Auckland in August 1996 were 4.3 percent lower than a year earlier.
In Wellington the August figures showed a 2.7 percent drop, while on an annual basis advertisements were down 19.4 percent in the capital.
In the South Island's main centre Christchurch job advertisements slid 2.7 percent in August and seven percent for the year.
The bank said the number of job advertisements in Christchurch and Auckland was still high compared to 1991 and 1992.
"As such there may still be some increase in numbers employed in these regions over the coming months, but growth prospects appear to be weakening."

The only region to show job advertisement growth in the year to August was Hawkes Bay (up 11.9 percent), while Manawatu was down 13.6 percent, Otago down 9.2 percent and Waikato down 2.2 percent. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
